CORRECTION: the H1 2026 column held figures this statement does not print (cost of sales 42,454,661 against a printed 42,451,370; gross profit 32,030,000 against 32,033,291; operating expenses 17,650,000 against 17,650,461; operating profit 14,380,000 against 14,382,831; profit before tax 11,700,000 against 11,699,397; income tax 3,978,398 against 3,977,795). The printed values replace them. Operating expenses is the printed administrative expenses 9,553,228, selling and distribution expenses 8,133,253, impairment of receivables 150,000 and net exchange difference 259,866 less other gains 445,886. Net finance costs is the printed finance costs 2,907,096 less the printed finance income 223,661. Ties exactly: revenue 74,484,661 less cost of sales 42,451,370 equals gross profit 32,033,291; profit before tax 11,699,397 less income tax 3,977,795 equals profit for the period 7,721,602. EPS stays blank: the printed earnings per share row does not reconcile to this period profit at any stable share count. | FILL 20261007_192730: Basic and diluted earnings per share 257 kobo for the six months ended 30 June 2026, Group Jan-Jun 2026 column, printed page 3 of the filing (column right edge 398pt equals the Jan-Jun 2026 column header edge). Ties: profit for the period 7,721,602 thousand divided by 3,004,513 thousand shares gives 2.5700 naira. source_note: H1 2026 column rebuilt 2026-10-06 from Fidson Healthcare Plc unaudited financial statements for the six months ended 30 June 2026 as reported (newtelegraphng.com, primebusiness.africa and nairametrics.com): Revenue N74.48bn (up 18.9%); cost of sales N42.45bn; gross profit N32.03bn (gross margin 43.01%); operating profit N14.38bn (operating margin 19.31%); Profit before tax N11.70bn; income tax N3.97bn; profit after tax N7.72bn. UNIT: NGN. Cost of Sales and Income Tax are DERIVED (Revenue minus Gross Profit; Profit Before Tax minus Net Profit) so the column ties to the published figures; Revenue and Net Profit are the exact figures already in the file. Net finance costs and Operating Expenses were not published as single lines, so both are left empty rather than approximated. Prior H1 2026 cell set was wrong: Cost of Sales had been back-filled as Revenue minus Net Profit and Gross Profit, Operating Profit and Profit Before Tax had all been set to the Net Profit figure. Identities checked: Revenue minus Cost of Sales = Gross Profit; Profit Before Tax minus Income Tax = Net Profit.

reconciliation_note: Gross Profit - Operating Expenses = Operating Profit (EBIT) does not hold in FY2025, FY2024: the filed operating profit is a subtotal that also carries operating income not shown as a separate row in this file, and it ties forward to Profit Before Tax. The figure is corroborated by the statement's own bridge and is shown unchanged.
